recognize_zh: 周邊血液中可見數顆中型芽細胞，核圓、染色質細緻、偶見小核仁，只有一圈深藍色無顆粒細胞質，形態為淋巴芽細胞；Ph+（BCR-ABL1）無法從形態判斷，須靠細胞遺傳或分子檢查。
features: Medium-sized blasts, about 1.5–2 times RBC diameter
High N:C ratio with narrow rim of basophilic agranular cytoplasm
Round to slightly irregular nuclei with fine chromatin
Small nucleoli visible in some cells; occasional cytoplasmic blebs
No granules or Auer rods; background RBCs unremarkable, platelets sparse
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows several circulating blasts of medium size with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, round to slightly irregular nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, small nucleoli in some cells, and a narrow rim of basophilic agranular cytoplasm. No Auer rods or granules are identified. Red cells are unremarkable and platelets appear decreased in this field. The morphology is that of lymphoblasts; the Philadelphia chromosome cannot be recognized morphologically. Findings are consistent with acute lymphoblastic leukemia, with BCR::ABL1 confirmation by cytogenetics, FISH or RT-PCR.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts may show granules, Auer rods and MPO positivity, whereas lymphoblasts are agranular and MPO negative with lymphoid markers by flow.
Morphologically identical; distinguished by a preceding chronic phase, basophilia and p210 BCR::ABL1 versus the p190 transcript typical of de novo Ph+ ALL.
Reactive lymphocytes have abundant cytoplasm that indents around RBCs and mature chromatin, lacking the fine blastic chromatin seen here.
